Title: Noctua Fan Swap on a Calnex Rb/GPS Frequency Reference
Description:
Since this will be the only source of this process on the Internet1, I figured I'd document a quick fan swap I did on a piece of test/reference equipment I'm running in my Atomic Clock Tower.
I took my Torx T10 screwdriver and popped off the top cover. The screws required some force to loosen, as they were all secured with Loctite.
The inside is simple and serviceable. There's a SpectraTime GRClok-1500, with an integrated timing-grade GPS module, and a stabilized 10 MHz output2.

Title: Unit tests mark territory more than squash bugs
Description:
I am a programmer who has worked a lot on hardware, and from that point of view, software testing looks horrible, since software is full of bugs. And you can explain this with, well, they push
programmers to ship buggy code since you can always fix the bugs later, and so the program is always full of bugs to be fixed
later — whereas with hardware, bugs are often (not
always!) catastrophic, so they have no choice but to let you fix them, even if it takes some time.

Title: The Half-Life of an Instruction
Description:
Two French examples. That is all it took.
I told DeepSeek’s larger model, V4 Pro, to translate every question into Russian. One earlier turn in which the assistant had answered in French was enough to make it slip 17 times in 100. Two, and it answered in French 90 times out of 90. Switch on thinking mode - the setting where the model writes out its reasoning before it answers - and the same model followed the instruction between 89 and 100 times in 100 at every number of turns I tested, up to 50.
